key_themes: AI capital expenditure surge rattles investors: Alphabet raises 2026 capex to $195-205B, triggering broad tech selloff
Q2 earnings divergence: defense and industrials surge while mega-cap tech and airlines disappoint
Oil spikes above $100/barrel on escalating Middle East tensions (Houthi attacks on Red Sea tankers)

stocks.discussion_driver: Tesla cratered 14.5% to $319.69, an 11-month low, after Q2 2026 earnings badly missed estimates ($0.33 non-GAAP EPS vs $0.55 expected). Capital expenditures surged 142% YoY to $5.79B and free cash flow turned deeply negative at -$1.09B, raising concerns about the pace of AI and robotics spending with no clear near-term payoff.
bull_case: Robotaxi and Full Self-Driving platform expansion could unlock a high-margin, recurring revenue stream with near-term city rollouts expanding globally
Energy storage segment (Megapack/Powerwall) growing 50%+ YoY could become a major earnings contributor independent of vehicle sales
bear_case: Q2 earnings miss and -$1.09B free cash flow signal severe execution risk while management keeps raising capex guidance
Valuation at 335x trailing P/E is difficult to justify given margin compression and slowing EV delivery growth

stocks.discussion_driver: Alphabet fell 6.55% to $319.70 despite Q2 2026 earnings beats (revenue $119.8B, Google Cloud up 82% YoY). The selloff was driven by management raising 2026 capex guidance to $195-205B, stoking fears of sustained negative free cash flow as AI infrastructure spending escalates. The move rippled across mega-cap tech, dragging Amazon and Microsoft lower.
bull_case: Google Cloud growing at 82% YoY is establishing a dominant enterprise AI platform with high-margin recurring revenue; operating income tripled to $6.6B at a 32.9% margin
Core search and advertising generating $100B+ annually with AI Overviews driving 19% search revenue growth provides a durable earnings floor as monetization expands
bear_case: Capex escalation to $195-205B in 2026 threatens free cash flow and may require debt issuance, limiting buybacks and dividends at the very moment AI ROI is unproven
Antitrust scrutiny and competition from Microsoft Copilot and OpenAI products could erode search market share over the next 2-3 years

stocks.discussion_driver: Lockheed Martin surged 11.4% to $573.21 after Q2 2026 results crushed expectations (EPS $7.94 vs $7.09 est.; revenue $20.06B vs $19.34B est.) and raised full-year revenue guidance to $79.75B-$81.75B. A $10.5B SOCOM logistics contract and $1.6B Navy F-35 spare parts order amplified confidence in the record order pipeline.
bull_case: Surging global defense budgets driven by NATO expansion and Middle East/Ukraine conflicts are building LMT's backlog to record levels, with demand outpacing production capacity
F-35 program provides decades of guaranteed revenue across 17 countries through ongoing upgrades, sustainment contracts, and spare parts demand
bear_case: Stock remains 17% below its 52-week high of $692 despite today's surge, suggesting the market has structural concerns about defense budget sustainability if geopolitical tensions ease
Analyst consensus is only Hold/Neutral (6 buy, 14 hold, 1 sell) implying limited further upside at current levels from a sell-side standpoint

stocks.discussion_driver: Intel reported Q2 2026 revenue of $16.1B (+25% YoY), the sharpest quarterly growth in nearly 15 years, with adjusted EPS of $0.42 doubling the $0.21 consensus. Q3 guidance of $15.8B-$16.8B also topped expectations. The stock closed regular trading at $102.72 and jumped roughly 9% after hours as investors cheered the broadest execution beat of Intel's foundry-led turnaround.
bull_case: AI PC and data center chip demand is driving Intel's first sustained multi-quarter revenue acceleration since 2021, validating the foundry-first strategy ahead of the Intel 18A node ramp
Intel 18A process node customer commitments suggest the foundry business could achieve meaningful revenue contribution in 2027, adding a high-margin growth vector
bear_case: Stock trades 28% below its 52-week high despite the strong beat; forward P/E of ~147x leaves virtually no margin for error in coming quarters
TSMC and AMD continue winning high-performance compute designs; Intel's server CPU market share recovery remains slow relative to elevated investor expectations

stocks.discussion_driver: Honeywell rose 5-6.3% to $247.68 after Q2 2026 earnings beat across the board (non-GAAP EPS $4.52 well above forecast; revenue $9.72B up 4.3% YoY) and management raised FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance with the midpoint above consensus. Multiple analysts lifted price targets post-earnings: Deutsche Bank to $263, Citigroup to $260, and Evercore upgraded to Outperform with a $275 target.
bull_case: Automation and building management systems are benefiting from global energy efficiency mandates and industrial reshoring, providing durable mid-single-digit organic growth with margin expansion
Post-spin-off portfolio simplification toward high-growth software and services segments should drive multiple expansion as business mix improves
bear_case: Stock sits only 4.8% below its 52-week high of $260.15 after today's surge, leaving limited near-term upside relative to most analyst price targets
Aerospace segment faces headwinds from airline sector weakness and oil prices above $100/barrel, which could temper demand for aerospace components and MRO services
